svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Second-order response for four damping ratios
svg.desc: Magnitude and phase of a second-order low-pass system against frequency divided by the natural frequency, from 0.1 to 10, for damping ratios 0.1, 0.3, 0.707 and 1. At the natural frequency the magnitude is +14 dB for 0.1, +4.4 dB for 0.3, -3 dB for 0.707 and -6 dB for 1, and every curve passes through -90 degrees. Lower damping gives a taller peak and a faster phase change. A table on the right lists the peak height and Q for each damping ratio.
svg.text: 2nd-order low-pass: the effect of damping ζ
Less damping: a taller peak and a
sharper phase drop. ζ = 0.707 is the
Butterworth case: no peak, −3 dB at fn.
